espresso.$description: Espresso — Page canvas and primary surface — warm coffee-black rather than pure black, the entire site sits on this

midnight-cocoa.$description: Midnight Cocoa — Deepest surface for footers and recessed bands — almost-black brown for slight layering below Espresso

warm-cream.$description: Warm Cream — Primary text and icon strokes — the only ink color across the system, reads as off-white parchment in dark contexts

soft-cream.$description: Soft Cream — Occasional light surface tint where near-white is needed (rare, secondary to Warm Cream)

walnut.$description: Walnut — Subtle hairline borders on dark surfaces — warm taupe that holds edges without competing with content

cedar.$description: Cedar — Neutral form states, badge text, and quiet UI feedback where color should stay understated. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

driftwood.$description: Driftwood — Muted helper text and secondary labels — warm gray that recedes against Espresso without disappearing

burnt-edge.$description: Burnt Edge — Faint internal border on cards and panels — barely-visible depth line on the dark canvas

amber-forge.$description: Amber Forge — Primary action fill, accent highlights, and the system signal color — the only chromatic accent; appears on filled CTAs, icon hover states, and section dividers. Pairs against Espresso for a heated-metal contrast that feels pressed-in and intentional

pp-neue-montreal.$description: Sole typeface across the entire system. PP Neue Montreal is a geometric humanist sans with a soft, slightly rounded terminal — more editorial than Inter, more clinical than GT America. Used at weight 400 for body and 500 for emphasis; no weight 600+ anywhere, which keeps the voice restrained and high-end. Display sizes (43–81px) use tight negative tracking (down to -1.13px) to lock letters into compact editorial blocks. Substitute with Inter (close) or Manrope (slightly warmer).
